references.text: Continuation of the rules about who may eat holy food: a priest's daughter who marries a foreigner cannot eat of the holy things, but if she becomes a widow, she may again eat of her father's food.
Describes what happens if someone eats holy food by mistake—they must make restitution and add one-fifth to it.
States that a foreigner shall not eat of the sin offering; only Aaron and his sons may do so.
Instructions that the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution offering are to be eaten in a clean place by the priest and his family.
Parallel legislation regarding who in the priest's household may eat of the holy gifts.
Mentions the toshav (resident alien) and sakir (hired worker) in another context, illustrating these categories of people in Israelite society.
Ezekiel's vision repeats the prohibition that foreigners (זָר) shall not enter the sanctuary.
